extracted.intended_audience: sponsors developing biological products, sponsors of biologics license applications (BLAs), and other interested parties
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for sponsors to provide information to FDA to support determination of the date of first licensure for a 351(a) biological product and eligibility for reference product exclusivity under section 351(k)(7) of the PHS Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of first licensure determination
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA must determine the date of first licensure for a biological product submitted under 351(a) to identify whether that product is eligible for a period of reference product exclusivity under 351(k)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of first licensure generally is the initial date the product was licensed in the U.S., but exclusions in 351(k)(7)(C) mean not every 351(a) licensure gives rise to its own exclusivity period. Sponsors may submit information (and should include an exclusivity claim in eCTD Module 1.3.5.3) to assist FDA with the determination. Determinations may be deferred if issues are scientifically, legally, or factually complicated, information is submitted late, incomplete, or FDA requests more data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from first licensure — supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 351(k)(7)(C), the date of approval of a supplement for the biological product that is the reference product is not considered a date of first licensure for purposes of exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an approval is for a supplement to an existing reference product, that approval date generally will not start a new exclusivity period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from first licensure — subsequent non‑structural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A subsequent application filed by the same sponsor/manufacturer (or a licensor, predecessor in interest, or other related entity) for a change (not including a modification to the structure of the biological product) that results in a new indication, route of administration, dosing schedule, dosage form, delivery system, delivery device, or strength is excluded from the date of first licensure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such changes (new indication, route, dosing schedule, dosage form, delivery system/device, or strength) generally do not create a new period of exclusivity when filed by the same or related entity, unless the change includes a structural modification that also changes safety, purity, or potency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — predecessor in interest
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA intends to interpret 'predecessor in interest' as in the 3‑year new drug exclusivity context: an entity the sponsor has taken over, merged with, or purchased, or that has granted the sponsor exclusive rights to market the biological product or exclusive rights to the data underlying the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes licensors, assignors, and joint venture partners depending on circumstances. Purchase of nonexclusive rights to a clinical investigation after completion is not sufficient. See 21 CFR 314.108(a) and related rules for analogous interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — licensor
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'licensor' is any entity that has granted the sponsor a license to market the biological product, regardless of whether the license is exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include entities that retain rights to develop, manufacture, or market the product and/or rights to intellectual property covering the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — other related entity
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'other related entity' generally includes entities where one owns, controls, or has the power to own or control the other (directly or through other entities), or entities under common ownership or control; may also include entities engaged in certain commercial collaborations related to product development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding relatedness FDA will consider ownership/control of the IND and BLA and the level of collaboration during the development program. Routine service contracts generally do not qualify unless they reflect common ownership or development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural modification criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a product includes a 'modification to the structure' of a previously licensed biological product to assess eligibility for a new exclusivity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should describe structural similarities and differences between the proposed product and any previously licensed product filed by the same sponsor or related entity. For protein products, include amino acid sequence differences, glycosylation patterns, tertiary structures, post‑translational events (including chemical modifications such as pegylation), infidelity of translation or transcription, and other principal structural molecular features. FDA will also consider whether the modified product affects the same molecular target as the previously licensed product. Use of a modified cell line does not alone establish a structural modification; sponsors should demonstrate the product is structurally modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in safety, purity, or potency standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A structural modification results in a change in safety, purity, or potency only if demonstrable data show measurable effects comparing the modified product to the previously licensed product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is case‑by‑case and generally based on sponsor‑submitted data, typically preclinical or clinical studies and relevant methods such as bioassays. Supporting information can reference data from the previously licensed product's 351(a) application. Evidence can include demonstration of a meaningful public health benefit, therapeutic advantage, or other substantial benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of change when molecular target differs
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA generally will presume that a structural modification has resulted in a change in safety, purity, or potency if the sponsor demonstrates the modified product affects a different molecular target than the original product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A molecular target includes receptors, enzymes, ion channels, structural or membrane transport proteins, nucleic acids, pathogens, etc. If different molecular target is shown, sponsor need not additionally prove change in safety/purity/potency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden when molecular target is the same
rubrics_metrics.description: If the modified product affects the same molecular target as the previously licensed product, the sponsor must provide data showing the structural changes result in a change in safety, purity, or potency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent such data, the date of licensure of the modified product generally will not be treated as a date of first licensure and the product will not be eligible for its own period of exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested listing of structurally related licensed products
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors should provide a list of all licensed biological products that are structurally related to the product subject to the 351(a) application, focusing on products that affect the same molecular target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include products that target different epitopes of the same molecular target. Where specific molecular targets are undefined, include products that share the narrowest characterizable target (pathway, cell type, tissue, or organ system). If no relevant previously licensed products exist, provide adequate justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested listing of products with sponsor/affiliate license history
rubrics_metrics.description: From the list of structurally related products, identify those for which the sponsor or an affiliate (including licensors, predecessors in interest, or related entities) is the current or previous license holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the definitions of predecessor/licensor/related entity provided in the guidance when compiling this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of structural differences to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific descriptions of structural differences between the proposed product and any relevant previously licensed products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For protein products, include changes in amino acid sequence, post‑translational events, infidelity of translation/transcription, glycosylation pattern differences, tertiary structure differences, and differences in biological activities. Biological activities can be important measures of structural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence linking structural differences to safety/purity/potency changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit evidence demonstrating changes in safety, purity, and/or potency between the proposed product and relevant previously licensed products, and explain how structural differences relate to those changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include preclinical/clinical data or bioassay results, and any comparative analyses; cite data from the earlier 351(a) application where relevant. Evidence may include meaningful public health or therapeutic advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended submission format and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA recommends including exclusivity information in the 351(a) application at submission or as correspondence/amendment; place exclusivity request in eCTD Module 1.3.5.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information can be submitted at initial filing, as correspondence, or as an amendment. Because determinations can be complex, timely and complete submission is advised to facilitate making the determination before licensure when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of exclusivity decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is evaluating options for making information publicly available regarding reference product exclusivity and dates of first licensure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a method for publication is determined, FDA will provide plans on its website.
